items.title: The product, Euclidean-metric and norm topologies on $\mathbb{R}^n$ agree, and for $n=1$ they agree with the real-line topology
Euclidean spheres and closed balls as subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$
Pseudocompact space: every continuous real-valued function has bounded image
A pseudocompact subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is bounded
A pseudocompact subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is closed
For a nonempty subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$, compactness, closedness and boundedness, pseudocompactness, and attainment of extrema by every continuous real-valued function are equivalent

Assuming countable choice and dependent choice, compactness, sequential compactness, countable compactness, limit point compactness, completeness and total boundedness, pseudocompactness, closedness and boundedness, and the extreme-value property are equivalent for nonempty subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$
For $n\ge 1$, every Euclidean closed ball and every Euclidean sphere of positive radius is compact
Polygonal paths and polygonally connected subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$
A finite concatenation of straight segments in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a continuous path
The points polygonally reachable from a fixed point form a clopen subset of every open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$
For an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$, connectedness, path-connectedness and polygonal connectedness are equivalent
Every connected component of an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is open and polygonally connected
$\mathbb{R}^n$ is polygonally connected, connected, locally path-connected and locally connected
$\mathbb{R}^n$ is locally compact and $\sigma$-compact
Every finite power of an at most countable set is at most countable
$\mathbb{Q}^n$ is a countable dense subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$, and rational open boxes form a countable basis
For $n\ge 2$, the punctured space $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$ is polygonally connected
Radial normalisation $x\mapsto x/\lVert x\rVert_2$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$

For $n\ge 1$, the map $H(x,t)=((1-t)+t/\lVert x\rVert_2)x$ is continuous on $(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\})\times[0,1]$, starts at $x$, ends at radial normalisation, fixes the unit sphere, and never reaches $0$
For $n\ge 2$, the sphere $S^{n-1}$ is path-connected and connected
FALSE: every connected subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is polygonally connected
$\mathbb{R}$ is not homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^n$ for any $n\ge 2$

title: The Topology of Euclidean Space — Examples

items.title: The Euclidean closed ball and sphere worked through the compactness equivalence chart
The open unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is bounded and not compact
$\mathbb{R}^n$ is closed and unbounded and is not compact for $n\ge 1$
The straight segment between two points of an open Euclidean ball stays in the ball
$GL_1(\mathbb{R})=\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ is disconnected, whereas $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ is polygonally connected
An infinite particular-point space is pseudocompact and not compact
Directed preorders and nets
A net is eventually or frequently in a subset of its codomain
Convergence and cluster points of a net in a topological space
Subnet via an eventually cofinal index map
Subnets preserve eventual properties and every limit of a net
A point is a cluster point of a net if and only if some subnet converges to it
A point lies in the closure of a set if and only if a net in the set converges to it
A map of topological spaces is continuous at a point if and only if it preserves every net converging to that point
A topological space is Hausdorff if and only if every net has at most one limit
The tail filter of a net
Convergence and cluster points of a filter on a topological space
A net and its tail filter have the same limits and cluster points
The canonical net indexed by the pairs $(A,x)$ with $A$ in a filter and $x\in A$
A filter and its canonical derived net have the same limits and cluster points
The tail-filter and derived-net constructions preserve convergence and cluster points in both directions
Universal net: eventually in every subset or eventually in its complement
A net is universal exactly when its tail filter is an ultrafilter, and the canonical net of an ultrafilter is universal
Every cluster point of an ultrafilter is a limit of that ultrafilter

Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, compactness is equivalent to every net having a cluster point, every net having a convergent subnet, every filter having a cluster point, and every ultrafilter converging
Every cluster point of a universal net is a limit of that net
The image of a universal net under any map is universal, and a continuous map preserves its limits
Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, every net has a universal subnet
Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, a space is compact if and only if every universal net converges
Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, an arbitrary product of compact Hausdorff spaces is compact
The compact Hausdorff product theorem uses the ultrafilter lemma, while the published arbitrary compact product theorem assumes the full Axiom of Choice
Fréchet–Urysohn spaces and sequential spaces
Assuming countable choice, every first countable space is Fréchet–Urysohn; in ZF every Fréchet–Urysohn space is sequential
FALSE: every subnet of a sequence is a subsequence

title: Convergence: Nets and Filters: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A neighbourhood-indexed net in $A$ converges to each point of $\overline{A}$
Finite partial sums of a real family form a net directed by inclusion

Assuming countable choice, a real family is summable as a finite-subset net if and only if it has countable support and its nonzero terms form an absolutely convergent series; its sum is independent of the enumeration
Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$ converges to the added point in the one-point convergent-sequence space
The coordinate-reading sequence in a compact binary cube has a convergent subnet but no convergent subsequence
In the cocountable topology on $\mathbb{R}$, a closure point outside $[0,1]$ is reached by a net in $[0,1]$ but by no sequence in $[0,1]$
The sequential fan is Fréchet–Urysohn and not first countable
Arens space $S_2$ is sequential but not Fréchet–Urysohn
Uniform space in the entourage formulation
Every uniformity has a base of symmetric entourages
The sets containing an entourage ball about each of their points form a topology
Separated uniformity: the intersection of all entourages is the diagonal
A uniformity is separated if and only if its induced topology is Hausdorff
Uniformly continuous map between uniform spaces
Every uniformly continuous map is continuous for the induced topologies
A metric generates an entourage uniformity whose induced topology and uniformly continuous maps are the usual metric notions, and this uniformity is separated
Uniform space in the uniform-cover formulation
Entourage uniformities and uniform-cover structures determine one another
A gauge of pseudometrics and the uniformity it generates
Assuming dependent choice, every entourage begins a decreasing symmetric sequence whose next triple composite lies in the preceding entourage
A normal sequence of entourages yields a uniformly continuous pseudometric with controlled dyadic balls
Assuming dependent choice, every entourage uniformity is generated by a gauge of uniformly continuous pseudometrics
Entourages and uniform covers give equivalent definitions of a uniform space in ZF, and under dependent choice they are also equivalent to gauges of pseudometrics
Cauchy filter in a uniform space
Every convergent filter on a uniform space is Cauchy
A Cauchy filter with a cluster point converges to that point
Complete uniform space: every Cauchy filter converges
Uniform embedding and uniform isomorphism
A Hausdorff completion of a uniform space and its canonical dense map
Every Cauchy filter canonically determines a unique minimal Cauchy filter coarser than it
The standard entourages on minimal Cauchy filters form a separated uniformity
The uniform space of minimal Cauchy filters is complete
The minimal Cauchy filters associated to points define a uniformly continuous dense canonical map
Every uniform space has a complete Hausdorff reflection with dense canonical image, and the canonical map is a uniform embedding exactly when the original uniformity is separated
Every uniformly continuous map into a complete Hausdorff uniform space extends uniquely across the Hausdorff completion; consequently completions are unique up to a unique uniform isomorphism
Totally bounded uniform space
Every ultrafilter on a totally bounded uniform space is Cauchy
Every compact uniform space is complete
Every compact uniform space is totally bounded
Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, every complete and totally bounded uniform space is compact
Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, a uniform space is compact if and only if it is complete and totally bounded
Every open cover of a compact Hausdorff space has a finite open star-refinement
The covers admitting an open refinement form a compatible uniform-cover structure on a compact Hausdorff space; in particular every open cover is uniform
A compact Hausdorff space carries exactly one compatible uniformity
Every continuous map from a compact Hausdorff space to a uniform space is uniformly continuous
A uniformity with a countable entourage base
A countable entourage base can be replaced in ZF by a decreasing symmetric base whose next triple composite lies in the preceding member
Every countably based uniformity is generated by one pseudometric, which is a metric exactly when the uniformity is separated
Uniformizable and separated-uniformizable topological spaces
Every uniformizable space is regular
Assuming dependent choice, every uniformizable space is completely regular
The topology of a completely regular space is induced by the gauge of its continuous $[0,1]$-valued pseudometrics
Assuming dependent choice, a topological space is uniformizable if and only if it is completely regular
Assuming dependent choice, a topological space is separated-uniformizable if and only if it is Tychonoff
Topological group: multiplication and inversion are continuous
Left and right translations and inversion in a topological group are homeomorphisms
The left and right uniformities of a topological group
The left and right uniformities of a topological group induce its topology, and inversion interchanges them
The upper and Roelcke uniformities generated from the left and right uniformities of a topological group
Every topological group is uniformizable, and assuming dependent choice it is completely regular
The pointwise and uniform-convergence uniformities on a function set $Y^X$
The uniform-convergence uniformity is finer than the pointwise uniformity, and they agree when the domain is finite

title: Uniform Spaces: the Three Definitions: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The usual metric entourages on $\mathbb{R}$ induce its usual topology and usual uniform continuity
The map $x\mapsto x/(1+|x|)$ is a uniformly continuous homeomorphism from $\mathbb{R}$ to $(-1,1)$ whose inverse is not uniformly continuous
FALSE: every uniformizable topology has a unique compatible uniformity
The left, right, upper and Roelcke uniformities of the additive topological group $\mathbb{R}$ all equal its metric uniformity
The functions $f_n(k)=1$ for $k\ge n$ and $0$ otherwise converge pointwise but not uniformly on $\mathbb{N}$
The closed unit interval has exactly one compatible uniformity, namely its usual metric uniformity
The $K$-topology on $\mathbb{R}$ is not uniformizable
An uncountable Cantor cube is compact Hausdorff and uniformizable but not first countable, hence not metrizable
